outcomeNote: mishna; R' Akiva's hesitation disputes no named party

segments.en: «MISHNA:» When an individual takes a vow, he renders an object forbidden to himself or to others as though it were a sacrificial offering; this parallels the act of consecrating an offering, which also renders an item forbidden for personal use by means of a verbal declaration. The most direct expression of a vow is when an individual says: This object is forbidden to me, or to others, like an offering. Additionally, the mishna states that «all substitutes» for the language «of vows are like vows.» Consequently, if one states that an object is forbidden to him like a konam instead of like an offering [korban], the vow takes effect, as konam is a substitute term for the word korban (see 10a).

segments.he: וַחֲרָמִים — כַּחֲרָמִים, וּשְׁבוּעוֹת — כִּשְׁבוּעוֹת, וּנְזִירוּת — כִּנְזִירוּת.
segments.en: Similarly, substitutes for the language of «dedications are like dedications,» substitutes for the language of «oaths are like oaths, and» substitutes for the language of «nazirite» vows «are like nazirite» vows. Therefore, if one declared a ḥerekh instead of a dedication [ḥerem], a shevuta instead of an oath [shevua], or proclaimed that he was becoming a nazik instead of a nazirite [nazir], his statement takes effect.

segments.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ ״מוּדְּרַנִי מִמָּךְ״, ״מוּפְרְשַׁנִי מִמָּךְ״, ״מְרוּחֲקַנִי מִמָּךְ״, ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹכֵל לָךְ״, ״שֶׁאֲנִי טוֹעֵם לָךְ״ — אָסוּר.
segments.en: With regard to «one who says to another: I am avowed from you,» or: «I am separated from you,» or: «I am distanced from you,» and he then says: «That» which «I eat» of «yours,» or: «That» which «I taste» of «yours,» even though he did not explicitly state that he is taking a vow or specify the nature of the vow, the object of his vow is nevertheless «forbidden.» His intention is understood based on his incomplete statement, known as an intimation of a vow, and his vow therefore takes effect.

segments.he: ״מְנוּדֶּה אֲנִי לָךְ״, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָיָה חוֹכֵךְ בָּזֶה לְהַחְמִיר.
segments.en: However, if he says: «I am ostracized from you,» which does not clearly declare any matter to be prohibited, «Rabbi Akiva was uncertain» about this halakha but was inclined «to rule stringently about this» and consider it a vow prohibiting the speaker from deriving benefit from his fellow.

moves.summary: substitute terms for vows are vows

moves.cueHe: רבי עקיבא היה חוכך בזה להחמיר
moves.summary: on 'I am ostracized from you' he leaned to stringency

positions.claim: substitutes for vows, dedications, oaths and naziriteship are like them; 'I am avowed/separated/distanced from you... that I eat of yours' is binding
'I am ostracized from you' — uncertain, inclined to rule stringently
